instruction: We represent Kiveth Interactive, Inc., the buyer in its proposed asset purchase from Zerex Forge Studios, LLC. Before we go back to the other side, Kiveth needs to know where the deal documents leave it exposed. Please review all six documents in the folder and send me a memo that lists each issue you find, where it appears (document and section), why it matters for Kiveth, and your recommended fix.

rubric.text: The response concludes that Seller's Section 3.9 Intellectual Property representations survive only 90 days after Closing, leaving Kiveth practically unable to bring IP infringement or title claims. It identifies this in the Asset Purchase Agreement (Section 1.1 definition of IP Survival Date and/or Section 9.1(a)), explains why this matters to Kiveth, and recommends a fix.

The response concludes that the Escrow Agreement's sole-and-exclusive-source-of-recovery clause controls. As a result, Kiveth's claims for Fundamental Representations and Excluded Liabilities are effectively capped at the $4,850,000 escrow and lost after escrow release. It identifies this in Escrow Agreement Section 6.2 and/or APA Section 11.9, explains why this matters to Kiveth, and recommends a fix.
hints: sole and exclusive source of recovery

rubric.text: The response concludes that because Kiveth is controlled by console maker Pellucid Systems, the sale triggers Vantrell's consent right under the Character License. It also concludes that this consent is not a Required Consent or closing condition, so Kiveth could be required to close without the franchise character rights. It identifies this in the Disclosure Schedule (Schedule 3.10(b) and/or Schedule 7.2(c)) and/or APA Section 4.6, explains why this matters to Kiveth, and recommends a fix.
hints: Controlled by a Hardware Platform Holder

rubric.text: The response concludes that the Lumen Engine License non-renewal deadline (September 2, 2026, 120 days before December 31, 2026) passed before the September 21, 2026 Agreement Date. As a result, Seller's non-renewal covenant cannot be performed and Kiveth would assume renewal-term minimum royalty guarantees (roughly $5.4 million). It identifies this in Disclosure Schedule 3.10(a) and/or APA Section 6.8, explains why this matters to Kiveth, and recommends a fix.

The response concludes that Kiveth's indemnity of Odalys Brennt exposes Kiveth to unlimited liability for pre-closing development claims that the APA allocates to Zerex. It identifies this in the Key Employee Agreement, Section 8.2, explains why this matters to Kiveth, and recommends a fix.
hints: whether arising before or after the Effective Date

rubric.text: The response states that the Escrow Amount is $4,850,000.
The response states that the escrow is released 15 months after the Closing Date.
The response is a memo addressed to the supervising partner.
The response presents the issues as separate entries. Each entry states the document and section where the issue appears, why it matters to Kiveth, and a recommended fix.
The response claims that Seller can still deliver a timely notice of non-renewal of the Lumen Engine License after the Agreement Date.
The response claims that Seller's Section 3.9 Intellectual Property representations are Fundamental Representations.
